_comment: Links out to other people's work, newest first. Two lists: "articles" and "podcasts". "image" is a file in assets/news/ OR a full URL, and "credit" captions it; omit both for a text card. Prefer a local copy in assets/news/ — a linked image breaks if the source moves it. The NIH one below is linked because nih.gov refuses command-line downloads; save it by hand and switch the path when convenient. Only use images you may: YME's own, licensed, or public domain work by US federal agencies (NSF, NIH, NASA, FDA).

articles.title: Device helps people with paralysis communicate
articles.note: A brain-computer interface that lets someone speak and gesture through an avatar at the same time.

articles.title: Improving lung cancer detection
articles.note: A protein-based MRI contrast agent, which is a chemistry problem solved to make an imaging problem easier.

articles.title: Innovative imaging tool could improve diagnosis and treatment of hearing loss
articles.note: Optical coherence tomography used during surgery to see inside the inner ear, one of the harder parts of the body to image.

articles.title: Smart bandage clears new hurdle: monitors chronic wounds in human patients
articles.note: The iCares bandage samples a wound and reads it with on-board sensors, now tested on patients rather than in a lab.

podcasts.title: The future of electronics goes beyond circuit boards
podcasts.note: Stretchable electronics, the groundwork for sensors that sit on skin rather than in a box.

podcasts.title: The hidden DNA code that controls your genes
podcasts.note: The regulatory layer above the genome, and where a lot of drug discovery now starts.

podcasts.title: Could holographic 3D printing be real?
podcasts.note: Printing a whole object at once instead of layer by layer, which changes how devices get made.

podcasts.title: Can prosthetic limbs feel touch?
podcasts.note: Building haptic feedback into upper-limb prosthetics, so a hand can report what it is touching.
